primary_paper.citation: Tokiwa, E. (2024). Cultural Influences on Personality Types: A Cluster Analysis of HEXACO Traits in Japan. Research Square preprint. DOI: 10.21203/rs.3.rs-5323735/v1. Posted 2024-10-31.

sample.demographics: NOT COLLECTED. Author explicitly notes gender, age, and region were not obtained. Demographic stratification is therefore impossible from this paper.

primary_paper.method: Ward's method + k-means (selected), compared against LPA (GMM) and spectral clustering. 7-cluster solution selected by elbow, AIC/BIC, S_Dbw, C-index, Generalized Dunn, Baker-Hubert Gamma, G(+), Silhouette, Cohen's kappa (.9388), Adjusted Rand Index (.8829).
primary_paper.scale_note: Centers reported as RAW mean on the 1-5 Likert scale (NOT z-scores). Sample-wide reference means (from descriptive stats): H~3.30, E~3.30, X=2.80, A~(approx 3.0), C~(approx 2.9), O=3.62. Use these to convert to z-scores if needed. SDs reported: H=.79, E=.89, X=.91; other domain SDs not explicitly stated in the excerpted text.

clusters.label: Reserved Type
clusters.description: Introverted, agreeable, slightly lower self-management. Modest, prioritizes social harmony but struggles with self-management. Author maps this onto the classic Overcontrolled prototype with Japanese-cultural emphasis on introversion and harmony.

clusters.label: Emotionally Sensitive Type
clusters.description: High emotional sensitivity, low extraversion, but high openness. Expresses emotions openly, strong creativity. Largest single cluster.

clusters.label: Conscientious Introvert Type
clusters.description: Highly conscientious, introverted, intellectually curious. High honesty and responsibility; prefers solitary, reflective activities. Author maps onto Resilient prototype with Japanese cultural overlay.

clusters.label: Extraverted Agreeable Type
clusters.description: Sociable, agreeable, excels in social interactions. Outgoing, cooperative, socially engaged. Flat profile, broadly above-average across factors.

clusters.label: Independent Type
clusters.description: High self-management, low agreeableness, lower honesty-humility. Self-disciplined and independent; may struggle with harmonious relationships. Closest to Undercontrolled but with high C; reflects modern individualistic shift in Japan.

clusters.label: Extraverted Stable Type
clusters.description: Sociable, emotionally stable, lower self-management. Confident, high social energy, but lower H and C. Resembles Gerlach et al. (2018) 'Self-Centered/Egocentric'.

clusters.label: Introverted Leader Type
clusters.description: Introverted but highly honest, agreeable, and open; leadership potential. Honest, flexible thinkers. Highest Openness in the sample.

reliability.note: Honesty-Humility alpha=.57 is low; author flags this as a limitation.

limitations: No demographics collected — cannot give sex- or age-conditioned cluster shares.
Cluster centers reported as raw Likert means, not z-scores; convert using sample means/SDs.
Single-author study from a private company (SUNBLAZE Co., Ltd.); not university-affiliated.

supplementary_papers.citation: Kase, T., Ueno, Y., Kaziuchi, D., & Shimamoto, K. (2018). Characteristics of Resilients, Overcontrollers, Undercontrollers, and the Other Type in Personality Prototypes: Based on Comparison of the Levels of Life Skills. Japanese Journal of Personality, 27(1), 79-81. DOI: 10.2132/personality.27.2.8
supplementary_papers.relevance: Japanese sample (university students). Big Five (NOT HEXACO). Hierarchical cluster analysis produced 4 clusters: Resilients, Overcontrollers, Undercontrollers, and 'Not Identifiables' (proposed as Japan-specific, low Extraversion + high Agreeableness). Resilients and Not Identifiables had better mental health than Overcontrollers and Undercontrollers. Cluster shares and centroid z-scores not retrieved in this search; would require article download.

supplementary_papers.citation: Daljeet, K. N., Bremner, N. L., Giammarco, E. A., Meyer, J. P., & Paunonen, S. V. (2017). Taking a person-centered approach to personality: A latent-profile analysis of the HEXACO model of personality. Journal of Research in Personality, 70, 241-251.
supplementary_papers.relevance: North American university sample (NOT Japan). HEXACO LPA gave 5 profiles: socially considerate, self-confident, goal-oriented, withdrawn, maladjusted. Replicated across two samples. Used as the comparison anchor in Tokiwa (2024).

supplementary_papers.citation: Espinoza, J. A., Daljeet, K. N., & Meyer, J. P. (2020). Establishing the structure and replicability of personality profiles using the HEXACO-PI-R. Nature Human Behaviour, 4(7), 713-724.
supplementary_papers.relevance: Largest HEXACO profile replication to date (>270,000 participants, mostly Western). Found 5 robust profiles: egocentric, flexible, disciplined, sociable, role model. International but Japan share unknown.

supplementary_papers.citation: Gerlach, M., Farb, B., Revelle, W., & Amaral, L. A. N. (2018). A robust data-driven approach identifies four personality types across four large data sets. Nature Human Behaviour, 2(10), 735-742.
supplementary_papers.relevance: N>1.5M, Big Five (not HEXACO), four types: Average, Reserved, Self-Centered (Egocentric), Role Model. Females more likely Average; Role Model probability rises sharply with age; Self-Centered more common in young males. Datasets are Western-centric; Japan-specific shares not reported.

demographic_findings.SelfCentered: young males > older adults; declines sharply after adolescence

supplementary_papers.citation: Kerber, A., Roth, M., & Herzberg, P. Y. (2021). Personality types revisited - a literature-informed and data-driven approach to an integration of prototypical and dimensional constructs of personality description. PLoS ONE, 16(1), e0244849.
supplementary_papers.relevance: German representative + longitudinal dataset (N=22,820). Big Five (not HEXACO). 5 types: Resilient, Overcontroller, Undercontroller, Reserved, Vulnerable-Resilient. Methodology directly adopted by Tokiwa (2024). Not Japan, but provides the procedural template and the 'vulnerable-resilient' addition.

supplementary_papers.citation: Robins, R. W., John, O. P., Caspi, A., Moffitt, T. E., & Stouthamer-Loeber, M. (1996). Resilient, overcontrolled, and undercontrolled boys: Three replicable personality types. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 70(1), 157-171.
supplementary_papers.relevance: Foundational ARC (Asendorpf-Robins-Caspi) typology. Western adolescents. Provides the canonical 3-type baseline that Kase (2018) replicated in Japan as 4 types (adding 'Not Identifiables').

usage_notes_for_checklist.recommended_prior: Use Tokiwa (2024) 7-cluster shares as the unconditional prior P(cluster) for a Japanese adult. The author did NOT collect demographics, so sex- and age-conditioned priors must be borrowed from Gerlach (2018) on a per-cluster basis (e.g., Extraverted Stable / Egocentric skews young male; Conscientious Introvert / Role-Model-like skews older).
usage_notes_for_checklist.z_score_conversion: centers_raw_1to5 are 5-point Likert means. To convert to z: z = (raw - sample_mean) / sample_sd. Sample means reported: H~3.30, E~3.30, X=2.80, O=3.62. SDs partially reported: H=.79, E=.89, X=.91. For A and C, SDs were not extracted from the available text — treat z-scores for those domains as approximate.
cultural_calibration_warnings: Tokiwa sample is online/self-selected; may over-represent digital-comfortable cohort.

Schmitt et al. (2008) cross-cultural baseline finds Japanese score high N (E in HEXACO), low C/X/A/O vs other nations — the absolute means here already reflect that and should NOT be re-shifted when comparing within-Japan individuals.
Honesty-Humility alpha=.57 — treat H-based cluster discrimination with caution.
